[[Rochester High School (Michigan)|Rochester]] ([[Rochester Hills, Michigan]]) | college = [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] (2013–2014) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = * All-SEC Second Team (2014) * SEC All-Freshman Team (2014) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2013 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2013]]) }} '''James Young''' (born August 16, 1995) is an American [[basketball]] player who recently completed his college career for [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]]. ==High school career== [[File:20130403 MCDAAG James Young slashing layup (3).JPG|thumb|left|upright|Young slashes for a layup in the [[2013 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]]]] Young attended both [[Troy High School (Michigan)|Troy High School]] in [[Troy, Michigan]] and [[Rochester High School (Michigan)|Rochester High School]] in [[Rochester Hills, Michigan]]. As a junior at Troy in 2011–12, Young averaged 25.1 points, 10.5 rebounds, 4.5 assists and 2.5 steals per game, earning first-team All-State honors from the Associated Press, Detroit News and Detroit Free Press. As a senior at Rochester in 2012–13, Young 27.2 points, 16.0 rebounds and 5.7 assists per game, going on to earn McDonald’s All-American honors.[http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/james_young_862039.html James Young Bio] On October 11, 2012, Young signed a [[National Letter of Intent|letter of intent]] to play for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|University of Kentucky]].{{cite web|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/story/2012-10-11/james-young-kentucky-basketball-recruiting-john-calipari|title=Kentucky lands James Young, its third top-10 recruit|work=SportingNews.com|date=October 12, 2012|accessdate=January 6, 2013}} ==College career== In his freshman season at Kentucky, Young finished second in the school's single-season freshman history with 82 made 3-pointers on the season. He went on to be named to the 2014 All-SEC second team and All-Freshman team. In 40 games (39 starts), he averaged 14.3 points, 4.3 rebounds and 1.7 assists in 32.4 minutes per game.[http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/james-young-1.html James Young Stats] On April 17, 2014, Young declared for the NBA draft, forgoing his final three years of college eligibility.[http://espn.go.com/nba/draft2014/story/_/id/10797286/james-young-kentucky-wildcats-declares-nba-draft James Young declares for draft] ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== *[http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/james_young_862039.html Kentucky Wildcats bio] {{Persondata | NAME = Young, James | ALTERNATIVE NAMES = | SHORT DESCRIPTION = American basketball player | DATE OF BIRTH = August 16, 1995 | PLACE OF BIRTH = Flint, Michigan | DATE OF DEATH = | PLACE OF DEATH = }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Young, James}} [[Category:1995 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:African-American basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players at the 2014 NCAA Men's Division I Final Four]] [[Category:Basketball players from Michigan]] [[Category:Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball players]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:Parade High School All-Americans (boys' basketball)]] [[Category:Shooting guards]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Flint, Michigan]]
